criteria.text: Identifies that the core platform was developed by contractor Yarrow Energy plc without a written IP assignment, so the Company may not own it, and recommends obtaining a confirmatory assignment as a condition to Closing.

Identifies the threatened $450,000 claim by Lowther Engineering Ltd recorded in the board minutes and that it is not disclosed against the litigation warranty (Warranty 7.1), recommending a specific indemnity or price protection.
Calculates the long-stop date as 2 May 2026 (120 days after signing on 2 January 2026) and identifies that expected clearance on 16 June 2026 falls after it, recommending an extension.

Identifies that the MAC carve-outs (general economic, industry-wide and pandemic changes) contain no 'disproportionate effect' exception, so the Buyer bears those risks even where the Company is disproportionately affected, and recommends adding one.

Identifies that the Oakhurst Technologies Ltd contract (Clause 14.2) allows termination on a change of control without consent, that the disclosure against Warranty 6.3 says there is no such provision, and that consent should be obtained as a condition to Closing.
Flags that the board minutes and the disclosure letter are inconsistent about litigation.
Lists a confirmatory IP assignment from Yarrow Energy plc as a required third-party action not yet obtained.
Gives a pinpoint citation (document name and section/clause number) for every issue or finding.
